speaker: Doctor
text: Where exactly in the knee is the pain located, and can you describe the nature of the sensation? Did you experience any specific injury or twisting motion when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you feel any instability, such as the knee "giving way," or have you noticed significant swelling since the injury? I would also like to assess your range of motion and check for tenderness along the patellar tendon and joint line.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain worsen when you climb stairs or squat, and do you feel any tightness in your quadriceps muscles? I would like to palpate the area to check for localized tenderness and assess your muscle strength.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the pain is localized to the medial tibial plateau inferior to the patella and worsens with activity, this presentation is highly suggestive of medial tibial stress syndrome (shin splints) rather than an intra-articular knee pathology. I will now assess for tenderness along the medial border of the tibia and check for any signs of muscle tightness in the gastrocnemius and soleus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, we can rule out structural damage like tears or meniscal injuries, pointing toward an overuse injury. I will now perform a physical exam to check for localized tenderness along the medial tibial border and assess for tightness in the calf muscles.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your description of pain over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella, combined with recent increased volleyball activity and normal imaging, this is consistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome. I will now assess for tenderness at the patellar facets and check for any quadriceps weakness or tightness. DIAGNOSIS READY: Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome
